questions.stem: On this posterior view of the heart, the highlighted vessels draining into the left atrium are clinically important in atrial fibrillation because they:

choices.label: A
choices.text: Supply the myocardium with coronary arterial blood

choices.label: B
choices.text: Return blood directly to the systemic circulation bypassing the heart

choices.label: C
choices.text: Carry deoxygenated blood to the right ventricle

choices.label: D
choices.text: Contain sleeves of atrial muscle that generate the ectopic triggers of AF

choices.label: E
choices.text: Are the site where the sinoatrial node normally resides

explanation.summary: The highlighted structures are the pulmonary veins entering the left atrium. Myocardial sleeves extending into these veins are the principal source of ectopic activity triggering AF, which is why they are the target of pulmonary vein isolation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The highlighted structures are the pulmonary veins entering the left atrium. Myocardial sleeves extending into these veins are the principal source of ectopic activity triggering AF, which is why they are the target of pulmonary vein isolation.

questions.stem: This 12-lead ECG shows an irregularly irregular ventricular rhythm with no discernible P waves and a fibrillating baseline. What is the rhythm?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Atrial flutter with fixed 2:1 conduction

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ventricular tachycardia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Normal sinus rhythm

choices.label: D
choices.text: Third-degree (complete) heart block

choices.label: E
choices.text: Atrial fibrillation

explanation.summary: Absence of organized P waves, a chaotic fibrillatory baseline, and an irregularly irregular R-R interval are diagnostic of atrial fibrillation, reflecting disorganized atrial activity with variable AV conduction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Absence of organized P waves, a chaotic fibrillatory baseline, and an irregularly irregular R-R interval are diagnostic of atrial fibrillation, reflecting disorganized atrial activity with variable AV conduction.

questions.stem: This 12-lead ECG with rhythm strip shows an irregularly irregular ventricular rhythm with no discernible P waves. What arrhythmia is depicted?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Atrial fibrillation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Atrial flutter

choices.label: C
choices.text: First-degree AV block

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sinus tachycardia

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ventricular tachycardia

explanation.summary: The absence of organized P waves combined with an irregularly irregular R-R interval is the hallmark of atrial fibrillation, caused by chaotic atrial electrical activity and variable AV nodal conduction.
explanation.whyCorrect: The absence of organized P waves combined with an irregularly irregular R-R interval is the hallmark of atrial fibrillation, caused by chaotic atrial electrical activity and variable AV nodal conduction.

questions.stem: This 3-D electroanatomic map of the left atrium shows ablation lesions arranged in rings around the openings of the pulmonary veins. What is the rationale for this lesion placement?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To interrupt accessory pathways of the mitral valve

choices.label: B
choices.text: To ablate the sinoatrial node and slow the ventricular rate

choices.label: C
choices.text: To create scar in the ventricles preventing tachycardia

choices.label: D
choices.text: To electrically isolate the pulmonary veins, the dominant source of ectopic triggers for atrial fibrillation

choices.label: E
choices.text: To destroy the AV node so a pacemaker can take over

explanation.summary: Ectopic foci near the pulmonary vein ostia commonly initiate AF. Encircling ablation lines electrically isolate the veins from the atrium, preventing these triggers from propagating and maintaining fibrillation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ectopic foci near the pulmonary vein ostia commonly initiate AF. Encircling ablation lines electrically isolate the veins from the atrium, preventing these triggers from propagating and maintaining fibrillation.
